Subject: PoC throughput / headroom ask

Hi Grace —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to scope a short PoC (4 weeks) to validate latency and cost before committing to dedicated capacity. A few quick details on our expected workload: average prompt ~60 tokens, average response ~120 tokens, sustained baseline ~2,500 tokens/sec with short bursts to ~7,500 tokens/sec for a few minutes several times per day.

Can you send a rough GPU sizing + SLA/headroom recommendation (tokens/sec mapping to GPUs, p95 latency expectations for 128-token responses) so we can factor into procurement? Also, what committed tiers look like (e.g., minimal reserved GPUs vs burst/fallback)?

If simpler, loop in whoever owns dedicated sizing — we want numbers today to share with finance.

— Ethan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Ethan Wallace <ethan@skybound.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PoC throughput / headroom ask — sizing details attached

Ethan / Grace / Marissa —

Quick technical sizing (conservative estimates based on our rw-13b-quant and rw-33b-q kernels with continuous batching and KV cache enabled). See attached CSV for line-by-line math. Highlights below assume 128-token responses and include typical batching efficiency for 50–200 concurrent streams.

1) rw-13b-quant (8-bit, optimized kernels) — per A100-80GB equivalent node:
   - Sustained throughput (mixed single-request arrival): ~2,800 tokens/sec
   - Sustained with warm KV and aggressive batching: up to ~3,500 tokens/sec
   - p95 latency for 128-token reply at target concurrency: ~220–320ms (depends on burst control)

2) rw-33b-q (mixed quant + kernel tuning) — per A100-80GB equivalent node:
   - Sustained throughput: ~1,600 tokens/sec
   - Warmed + batched: ~2,200 tokens/sec
   - p95 latency for 128-token reply: ~280–420ms

Sizing recommendations for Skybound baseline 2,500 tokens/sec:
   - Option A (cost-sensitive, rw-13b-quant): 1 node provides ~3.5k TPS (with warmed cache). Recommend 1 reserved GPU node + 1 hot-standby for burst absorb (committed = 1, allowed burst to 2 via autoscale).
   - Option B (higher-quality, rw-33b-q): 2 nodes reserved to hit baseline with appropriate headroom (2 x 2.2k ~= 4.4k TPS warmed). Add 1 burst node for 30% headroom to survive 7.5k spikes (short duration).

Headroom & SLA mapping (target: p95 < 350ms for 128 tokens):
   - Maintain a warmed KV cache and 15–20% batching headroom. For Option A, with the additional hot-standby and autoscale policy we project p95 ~280ms typical and sub-400ms under 7.5k short bursts.

Operational notes / risks:
   - Cold-starts (cache empty) increase tail latency significantly — use prefix warming for anticipated sessions.
   - If Skybound wants strict sub-200ms p95, we need additional reserved capacity or smaller model variant for latency-critical endpoints.

Attachments: detailed_sizing_breakdown.csv — includes tokens->GPU math, cost delta examples (on-demand vs committed), and a short runbook for KV cache warm strategies.

Happy to walk through the numbers on Thu; if you want faster turnaround I can prepare an alternate sizing that trades 20% more cost for lower p95.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Thanks Karthik — that's helpful. A few clarifications to narrow the model choice: 

- Typical prompt 60 tokens, typical response 120 tokens (we already indicated)
- Peak bursts are short (1–5 minutes) but can reach 7.5k TPS as I said; sustained peaks are rare
- We have two classes of endpoints: interactive (tight latency — target p95 < 300ms) and background (batchable, latency-tolerant).

For the PoC, we care most about proving the interactive endpoint under the interactive SLA. Looks like Option A (rw-13b-quant) might be the sweet spot if warmed and with standby/burst nodes.

Commercially — what do the committed tiers look like for "1 reserved GPU + hot standby autoscale" vs "2 reserved GPUs + 1 burst"? Can Marissa send a sketch of commitment tiers + associated discounts and burst pricing? Also we need a DocuSign for the PoC agreement (4 weeks, fixed price) — can you drop that link?

Appreciate it,
Ethan
